double_counting_risk.risk: REAL and must be designed out before any WhatConverts upload starts flowing.
double_counting_risk.mechanism: GTM already fires a WEBPAGE form conversion (6885463625). If WhatConverts also uploads the same form lead to 7643656486 (UPLOAD_CLICKS, category CONTACT), one lead becomes two Primary conversions from two different sources. Today the risk is dormant only because WhatConverts uploads nothing.
double_counting_risk.resolution: Split responsibility by channel, not by tool: GTM owns FORM conversions, WhatConverts owns CALL conversions. Concretely - 6885463625 stays the single Primary form action; 7643656486 'WC Lead' is scoped to calls or set Secondary so it can never double-count a form; 7643656075 'WC Calls' becomes the authoritative Primary QUALIFIED-CALL action once uploads work.
double_counting_risk.deduplication_method: Every WhatConverts upload must carry the WhatConverts lead ID as the order/transaction ID, with the original gclid and the original click timestamp. Maintain an uploaded-lead-ID ledger and reject repeats. GTM form conversions dedupe independently on the Gravity Forms entry ID.

target_architecture.why_not_a_duration_rule: Ads are eligible 24/7 while staff are present roughly 08:00-16:00, and unanswered calls reach voicemail. A voicemail pickup is a connection and a message easily exceeds any duration threshold, so duration cannot define a qualified call.
